gist.label: Days 1–28 treatment / 14-day break
gist.prescription_note: No automatic prophylactic prescription is populated for this oral schedule. Agree individual nausea, bowel, skin and other symptom support.
additional_support: Swallow the prescribed capsules with water, with or without food. Take at a consistent time each treatment day. Use the written calendar to distinguish treatment days from the planned break.
Skip a missed sunitinib dose and take the next scheduled dose at the usual time. Do not take an extra or double dose. Ask the team about vomiting or repeated missed doses.

No routine separate premedication is specified. This oral schedule has minimal-to-low emetogenic potential; symptom medicines are prescribed individually. Ask for a hand-foot skin-care plan and early diarrhoea support. Treat blood-pressure or thyroid problems as prescribed. Tell the team before surgery, dental procedures or starting any new medicine.

Confirm the exact calendar and dose strength before each cycle. Review all prescription, non-prescription and herbal products, especially the liver enzyme cytochrome P450 3A4 interactions; avoid grapefruit and St John’s wort. Keep a blood-pressure and symptom record if your team asks.

Keep tablets or capsules in their supplied packaging, away from children, and follow the pharmacy storage instructions. Do not share medicines or alter the dose yourself. Ask the pharmacy before crushing, opening or dispersing a medicine; formulation-specific instructions differ. Return unused treatment to the pharmacy.

gist.label: Days 1–21 treatment / 7-day break
gist.prescription_note: No automatic prophylactic prescription is populated for this oral schedule. Agree individual nausea, bowel, skin and other symptom support.
additional_support: Swallow tablets whole with water after a light, low-fat meal, at a consistent time. Your pharmacy supplies the written food and dose instructions for the product you receive.
Take a missed dose when remembered on the same day. Do not take two doses on one day. Do not take extra tablets after vomiting; contact the team if vomiting continues.

No routine separate premedication is specified; oral emetogenic potential is minimal-to-low. Start the agreed hand-foot skin-care measures and report painful areas early. Use prescribed diarrhoea, nausea, blood-pressure or thyroid treatment. Tell the team before surgery or dental procedures because healing may be affected.

Confirm that both prior imatinib and sunitinib treatments have been reviewed. Reconcile all prescription, non-prescription and herbal products, including warfarin and the liver enzyme cytochrome P450 3A4 interactions; avoid grapefruit and St John’s wort. Agree liver-test and blood-pressure appointments before starting.

Keep tablets or capsules in their supplied packaging, away from children, and follow the pharmacy storage instructions. Do not share medicines or alter the dose yourself. Ask the pharmacy before crushing, opening or dispersing a medicine; formulation-specific instructions differ. Return unused treatment to the pharmacy.
